newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech gov to cut up to CZK30 bln in spending-paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech gov to cut up to CZK30 bln in spending-paper.

text.p: The Czech government will announce budget cuts of almost 30 billion crowns as part of an economic revival package to be unveiled on Wednesday, mass-circulation daily Mlada Fronta Dnes said.
"It will be a little less than 30 billion crowns," the paper quoted Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik as saying.

The government was meeting on Wednesday morning to give its final approval to the package which should also include wage restrictions in the state sector, capital market regulation changes, and measures to slow rapidly growing trade and current account deficits.
Government and central bank officials have repeatedly ruled out a devaluation of the crown, and spoken against an import surcharge as ways to close the trade gap.
Tax cuts and measures aimed at stricter prosecution of economic crimes are also expected, as well as an acceleration of the privatisation process.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus is expected to announce the measures at a news conference scheduled for 3 p.m. (1300 GMT).
Czech National Bank (CNB) officials have said the CNB would wait for market reaction to the government measures before considering any changes to monetary policy.
But on Tuesday, Governor Josef Tosovsky declined to clearly rule out an interest rate cut, despite comments from CNB board member Jan Vit at the weekend that a cut was not imminent.

The 1997 state budget was approved as balanced with revenues and expenditures at 549.1, but it had fallen into an 8.5 billion deficit after the first three months of the year due to lagging tax collection and a slowdown in the economy.
